blocks.title: Material
blocks.text: A material is any substance or mixture of substances that makes up a physical object of daily-life or industrial importance, for example plastics, metals, ceramics and building materials.

Materials have useful thermal, mechanical (for example hardness and elasticity) and chemical properties. These properties are understood through the material's composition, the nature of its chemical bonds and its microstructure. A material is chosen for a particular use according to its physical, chemical, mechanical, electrical and thermal characteristics. The main classes are metals and alloys, ceramics, polymers, composites and semiconductors.

blocks.alt: Five coloured cards. Metals and alloys: hard, strong, malleable, ductile, good conductors; steel in bridges, aluminium in aircraft, copper in wires. Ceramics: silicates and oxides, hard but brittle, high melting, insulators; bricks, porcelain, glass, alumina spark plugs. Polymers: large molecules from small units. Composites: a matrix holding a reinforcement; fibreglass, carbon fibre. Semiconductors: controllable conduction; Si, GaAs, GaN.
blocks.caption: Classes of materials (original diagram summarising topic 31.1).
blocks.long_description: Each class of material has typical properties that suit certain uses. A single device such as a phone uses several classes together.

blocks.prompt: Which three things help us understand the properties of a material?
blocks.explanation: Its composition, the nature of its chemical bonds and its microstructure.

items: A material makes up an object of daily-life or industrial importance.
Properties depend on composition, bonding and microstructure.
